newsitem.title: USA: Redwoods announcement set for Saturday.
newsitem.headline: Redwoods announcement set for Saturday.

text.p: The results of last-minute negotiations to prevent a timber firm from logging thousands of acres of pristine northern California redwoods will be announced Saturday, a spokeswoman for a senator said Friday.
"The four negotiators will discuss the status of the negotiations at 10 a.m. Saturday," said Susan Kennedy, press secretary to Sen. Dianne Feinstein, a California Democrat.

The negotiators have been working to prevent loggers going into the forests as soon as Monday to begin "salvage logging" of dead trees. Environmentalists say that would rip apart the virgin redwood groves.

Feinstein negotiated with Deputy Interior Secretary John Garamendi, California State Resources Secretary Doug Wheeler and Charles Hurwitz, the Texas financier who heads MAXXAM Inc., an energy company that owns the land in rural Humboldt County.
Pacific Lumber Co., a unit of MAXXAM, agreed to delay the start of logging for two weeks in the 3,000-acre (1,200-hectare) Headwaters area and five smaller groves.
Environmentalists argue that 60,000 acres (24,000 hectares) of the area should be protected, saying it encompasses an ecosystem needed to preserve endangered fish and birds.
The negotiations center on the Headwaters area, a buffer zone of 1,500 acres (600 hectares) and about 1,800 to 3,000 acres (700-1,200 hectares) included in the other parcels.
